results.title: Brauer–Fowler theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a function $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every finite nonabelian simple group $G$ and every element $t \in G$ of order $2$, with centralizer $C_G(t)$ in $G$, the order of $G$ satisfies $|G| \le f(|C_G(t)|)$.

Then $G$ is isomorphic to the alternating group $A_7$, or to the projective special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ for some power $q = p^k$ of an odd prime $p$ with…

results.title: 2-closed actions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An action of a group $G$ on a set $\Omega$ is $2$-closed when every permutation $\sigma$ of $\Omega$ that preserves each $G$-orbit on ordered pairs (that is, for all $\alpha, \beta \in \Omega$ some $g \in G$ satisfies $\sigma(\alpha) = g \alpha$ and $\sigma(\beta) = g \beta$) is induced by an element of $G$: there is $g \in G$ with $\sigma(\omega) = g \omega$ for all $\omega \in \Omega$.

results.title: Totally 2-closed groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is totally $2$-closed when every faithful action of $G$ on a set $\Omega$ is $2$-closed; equivalently, in each faithful permutation representation of $G$ on a set $\Omega$, $G$ is the largest subgroup of $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ preserving each of its orbits on $\Omega^2$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 20.1 (insoluble totally 2-closed groups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, asked by M. Arezoomand, M. A. Iranmanesh, C. E. Praeger and G. Tracey, that there exists a finite group $G$ that is not soluble, is totally $2$-closed, and has a nontrivial nilpotent normal subgroup (equivalently, a nontrivial Fitting subgroup).

results.title: A finite insoluble totally 2-closed group with nontrivial Fitting subgroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exists a finite group $G$ that is not soluble, is totally $2$-closed, and has a nontrivial nilpotent normal subgroup (equivalently, a nontrivial Fitting subgroup).

results.title: The $2$-closure of a permutation group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a subgroup $G$ of the symmetric group $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, the $2$-closure $G^{(2)}$ of $G$ is the subgroup of $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ generated by the permutations $\sigma$ that map every pair of points into its $G$-orbit, that is, such that for all $\alpha, \beta \in \Omega$ there is $g \in G$ with $g(\alpha) = \sigma(\alpha)$ and $g(\beta) = \sigma(\beta)$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 19.67
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every finite set $\Omega$ and every solvable subgroup $G$ of the symmetric group $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, every composition factor of the $2$-closure $G^{(2)}$ of $G$ is cyclic or isomorphic to the alternating group $A_n$ for some natural number $n$.

results.title: Characteristic of the residue field of a local ring
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `(p : A)` lies in the maximal ideal of a local ring `A`, the residue field has characteristic `p`: `p` maps to zero in the residue field.

results.title: Quotient of a local ring by a proper ideal is local
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A quotient of a local ring by a proper ideal is local. Mathlib uses this fact inline (via `IsLocalRing.of_surjective'`), but does not package it as a standalone lemma.

results.title: Floor sequence parity count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the floor sequence parity count $\mathcal{F}_n$ is the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ for which $\lfloor n/k \rfloor$ is odd (OEIS A059851).

results.title: The floor sequence parity count at $10$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $\mathcal{F}_{10}$ of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le 10$ for which $\lfloor 10/k \rfloor$ is odd equals $7$: the quotients $\lfloor 10/k \rfloor$ for $k = 1, \dots, 10$ are $10, 5, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1$, and seven of them are odd.

results.title: Ceiling parity count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the ceiling parity count $\mathcal{C}_n$ is the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ for which $\lceil n/k \rceil$ is odd (OEIS A330926).

results.title: The ceiling parity count at $9$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ceiling parity count $\mathcal{C}_9$, the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le 9$ for which $\lceil 9/k \rceil$ is odd, equals $5$.

results.title: Rounding sequence parity count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the rounding sequence parity count $\mathcal R_n$ is the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ for which the nearest integer to $n/k$ is odd, where half-integers are rounded up: the nearest integer to a rational number $x$ is taken to be $\lfloor x + 1/2 \rfloor$.

results.title: The rounding sequence parity count at $10$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $\mathcal{R}_{10}$ of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le 10$ for which the nearest integer to $10/k$ (half-integers rounded up) is odd equals $7$.

results.title: Every term is counted modulo one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary:
For a natural number $n$, real numbers $\alpha$ and $
u$, an integer $r$ and a natural number $m$, let $\mathcal N_{n,\alpha,
u,r,m}$ be the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ such that $\lfloor (n -

results.title: Counting large terms of the floor sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k \ge 1$, exactly $\lfloor n/k \rfloor$ of the integers $d$ with $1 \le d \le n$ satisfy $\lfloor n/d \rfloor \ge k$; that is, exactly $\lfloor n/k \rfloor$ terms of the floor sequence $\lfloor n/1 \rfloor, \dots, \lfloor n/n \rfloor$ are at least $k$.

results.title: The floor parity count as an alternating sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathcal{F}_n$ be the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ for which $\lfloor n/k \rfloor$ is odd. For every natural number $n$, $\mathcal{F}_n = \sum_{d=1}^{n} \lfloor n/d \rfloor (-1)^{d+1}$.

results.title: The floor parity count through the divisor summatory function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\tau(m)$ be the number of positive divisors of $m$, let $D(x) = \sum_{1 \le m \le x} \tau(m)$, and let $\mathcal{F}_n$ be the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ for which $\lfloor n/k \rfloor$ is odd. For every natural number $n$, $\mathcal{F}_n = D(n) - 2D(n/2)$, where $D(n/2) = D(\lfloor n/2 \rfloor)$.

results.title: Odd floor quotients as a hyperbolic lattice-point difference
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the floor sequence parity count $\mathcal{F}_n$ equals the number of integer pairs $(x, y)$ with $x, y \ge 1$ and $n/2 < xy \le n$ minus the number of integer pairs $(x, y)$ with $x, y \ge 1$ and $xy \le n/2$.

results.title: Dirichlet's asymptotic for the divisor summatory function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\tau(m)$ be the number of positive divisors of $m$, let $D(x) = \sum_{1 \le m \le x} \tau(m)$ for real $x$, and let $\gamma$ be the Euler–Mascheroni constant. There is a real constant $C$ such that $|D(x) - (x \log x + (2\gamma - 1)\, x)| \le C \sqrt{x}$ for every real $x \ge 1$.

results.title: Asymptotics of the floor parity count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathcal{F}_n$ be the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ for which $\lfloor n/k \rfloor$ is odd. There is a real constant $C$ such that $|\mathcal{F}_n - n \log 2| \le C \sqrt{n}$ for every integer $n \ge 1$, and $\mathcal{F}_n / n \to \log 2$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Ceiling parity count from the floor parity count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $m$, let $\mathcal{C}_m$ and $\mathcal{F}_m$ be the numbers of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le m$ for which $\lceil m/k \rceil$, respectively $\lfloor m/k \rfloor$, is odd. Then for every natural number $n$, $\mathcal{C}_{n+1} = (n + 1) - \mathcal{F}_n$.

results.title: Asymptotics of the ceiling parity count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathcal{C}_n$ be the number of integers $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ for which $\lceil n/k \rceil$ is odd. There is a real constant $C$ such that $|\mathcal{C}_n - (1 - \log 2)\, n| \le C \sqrt{n}$ for every integer $n \ge 1$, and $\mathcal{C}_n / n \to 1 - \log 2$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Square-root bound for the number of divisors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the number of positive divisors of $n$ is at most $2\sqrt{n}$. For $n = 0$ the set of divisors is taken to be empty, so the bound holds trivially.

results.title: Counting large terms of the rounded quotient sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. Every $d$ with $1 \le d \le n$ satisfies $\lfloor n/d + 1/2 \rfloor \ge 1$, and for every integer $k \ge 2$ the number of $d$ with $1 \le d \le n$ and $\lfloor n/d + 1/2 \rfloor \ge k$ is $\lfloor 2n/(2k-1) \rfloor$.

results.title: Alternating-sum formula for the rounding sequence parity count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the rounding sequence parity count $\mathcal{R}_n$ satisfies $\mathcal{R}_n = -n + \sum_{d=1}^{n} (-1)^{d+1} \lfloor 2n/(2d-1) \rfloor$.

results.title: Divisor-sum formula for the rounding sequence parity count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a positive integer $k$ and $r \in \{1, 3\}$, let $d_{r,4}(k)$ be the number of positive divisors of $k$ congruent to $r$ modulo $4$. Then for every natural number $n$, the rounding sequence parity count $\mathcal{R}_n$ satisfies $\mathcal{R}_n = -n + \sum_{k=1}^{2n} (d_{1,4}(k) - d_{3,4}(k))$.

results.title: Jacobi's formula for the number of representations as a sum of two squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the number $r_2(n)$ of pairs $(a, b) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ with $a^2 + b^2 = n$ equals $4\,(d_{1,4}(n) - d_{3,4}(n))$, where $d_{r,4}(n)$ is the number of positive divisors of $n$ congruent to $r$ modulo $4$.

results.title: Lattice points in the disc of radius $\sqrt{2n}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the number of pairs $(x, y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ with $x^2 + y^2 \le 2n$ equals $4\,\mathcal{R}_n + 4n + 1$, where $\mathcal{R}_n$ is the number of $k \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ for which the nearest integer to $n/k$, with half-integers rounded up, is odd. At $n = 0$ both sides are $1$.

results.title: The rounding sequence parity count drops by at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the rounding sequence parity count $\mathcal{R}$ satisfies $\mathcal{R}_{n+1} \ge \mathcal{R}_n - 1$.

results.title: Gauss's bound for lattice points in a disc
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a constant $C$ such that for every real $x \ge 1$, the number $N(x)$ of integer pairs $(a, b)$ with $a^2 + b^2 \le x$ satisfies $|N(x) - \pi x| \le C \sqrt{x}$.

results.title: Asymptotic density of odd rounded quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a constant $C$ such that the rounding sequence parity count $\mathcal{R}_n$ satisfies $|\mathcal{R}_n - (\pi/2 - 1)n| \le C\sqrt{n}$ for every natural number $n \ge 1$; moreover $\mathcal{R}_n / n \to \pi/2 - 1$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Stern-Brocot generations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The $n$-th Stern-Brocot generation $F_n$ is a finite set of intervals $[a/b, c/d]$, each stored as the quadruple $(a, b, c, d)$ of natural numbers. It is defined by $F_0 = \{[0/1, 1/1]\}$, and $F_{n+1}$ is obtained by replacing each $[a/b, c/d] \in F_n$ with its two mediant halves $[a/b, (a + c)/(b + d)]$ and $[(a + c)/(b + d), c/d]$.

results.title: The first two Stern-Brocot generations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Writing $[a/b, c/d]$ for the quadruple $(a, b, c, d)$, the first two Stern-Brocot generations are $F_1 = \{[0/1, 1/2], [1/2, 1/1]\}$ and $F_2 = \{[0/1, 1/3], [1/3, 1/2], [1/2, 2/3], [2/3, 1/1]\}$.

results.title: Recurrence for the Stern-Brocot generations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the generation $F_{n+1}$ is the union, over all intervals $[a/b, c/d] \in F_n$, of the two mediant halves $[a/b, (a + c)/(b + d)]$ and $[(a + c)/(b + d), c/d]$, where each interval $[x/y, z/w]$ is stored as the quadruple $(x, y, z, w)$.

results.title: Length bound for the Stern-Brocot generations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, every interval $[a/b, c/d]$ of the $n$-th Stern-Brocot generation $F_n$, that is, every quadruple $(a, b, c, d) \in F_n$, satisfies $c/d - a/b \le 1/(n + 1)$.

results.title: Multinomial mass function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The multinomial mass function: the probability `N! / ∏ᵢ xᵢ! · ∏ᵢ pᵢ ^ xᵢ` that `N` independent throws, landing in cell `i` with probability `pᵢ`, produce the cell counts `x`; it is `0` unless `∑ᵢ xᵢ = N`. The formula is a polynomial in `p` and is defined for every real vector `p`; it is a probability mass function when `p` is a probability vector (`0 ≤ pᵢ`, `∑ᵢ pᵢ = 1`), which the normalization theorems assume. The…

results.title: Nonnegativity of the multinomial mass function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The multinomial mass function is nonnegative for a nonnegative vector `p`.

results.title: Multinomial mass vanishes off the simplex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The multinomial mass function vanishes off the simplex `∑ᵢ xᵢ = N`.

results.title: Multinomial mass formula on the simplex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the simplex the multinomial mass is `N! / ∏ᵢ xᵢ! · ∏ᵢ pᵢ ^ xᵢ`.

results.title: Support of the multinomial mass lies in the antidiagonal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The multinomial mass function vanishes outside the finite set `piAntidiag univ N` of count vectors with total `N`: the support is contained in the antidiagonal. Equality of the support with the antidiagonal needs all `p i > 0` (e.g. for `p = (1, 0)`, `N = 1` the vector `(0, 1)` is in the antidiagonal but has mass `0`).

results.title: Multinomial theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `∑ₓ P(x) = (∑ᵢ pᵢ) ^ N` for every real vector `p`.

results.title: Normalization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `∑ᵢ pᵢ = 1` the multinomial masses sum to one.

results.title: Multinomial distribution as a probability mass function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The multinomial law of `N` throws with cell probabilities `p` (a probability vector), as a probability mass function on count vectors `ι → ℕ`.

results.title: Mass of the multinomial distribution at a count vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mass of the multinomial PMF at `x` is `multinomialReal N p x`.

results.title: Mean, polynomial form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `∑ₓ xᵢ P(x) = N pᵢ (∑ⱼ pⱼ) ^ (N - 1)` for every real vector `p`.

results.title: Second factorial moment, polynomial form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `i ≠ j`, `∑ₓ xᵢ xⱼ P(x) = N (N - 1) pᵢ pⱼ (∑ₗ pₗ) ^ (N - 2)` for every real vector `p`.

results.title: Second factorial moment, polynomial form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `∑ₓ xᵢ (xᵢ - 1) P(x) = N (N - 1) pᵢ² (∑ₗ pₗ) ^ (N - 2)` for every real vector `p`.

results.title: Mean
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a probability vector (`0 ≤ pᵢ`, `∑ⱼ pⱼ = 1`), `E Xᵢ = N pᵢ`. The underlying `sum_mul_multinomialReal_eq` is a polynomial identity holding for every real `p`.

results.title: Mixed second moment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a probability vector and `i ≠ j`, `E[Xᵢ Xⱼ] = N (N - 1) pᵢ pⱼ`.

results.title: Second factorial moment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a probability vector, `E[Xᵢ (Xᵢ - 1)] = N (N - 1) pᵢ²`.

results.title: Covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a probability vector (`0 ≤ pᵢ`, `∑ₗ pₗ = 1`), `Cov(Xᵢ, Xⱼ) = ∑ₓ (xᵢ - N pᵢ) (xⱼ - N pⱼ) P(x) = N (δᵢⱼ pᵢ - pᵢ pⱼ)`; in particular `Var Xᵢ = N pᵢ (1 - pᵢ)` and `Cov(Xᵢ, Xⱼ) = -N pᵢ pⱼ` for `i ≠ j`.

results.title: Poisson conditioning
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `Xᵢ ~ Po(λᵢ)`, `i ∈ ι`, be independent Poisson counts with `∑ᵢ λᵢ > 0`. Given their total `∑ᵢ Xᵢ = N`, the count vector is multinomial with `N` throws and cell probabilities `λᵢ / ∑ⱼ λⱼ`: `P(X = x | ∑ᵢ Xᵢ = N) = multinomialReal N (λ / ∑ λ) x`.

results.title: Poisson conditioning, two cells
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For independent `X ~ Po(a)` and `Y ~ Po(b)` with `a + b > 0`, the law of `X` given `X + Y = N` is binomial `Bin(N, a / (a + b))`.

results.title: Balanced biclique instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of BALANCED BICLIQUE is a triple $(n, es, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).

results.title: Graph of a balanced biclique instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The graph of a balanced biclique instance $(n, es, K)$ is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ belongs to $es$.

results.title: Well-formed balanced biclique instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A balanced biclique instance $(n, es, K)$ is well formed when the entries of the list $es$ are distinct and every pair $(u, v)$ in $es$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \neq v$ and $(v, u) \notin es$.

results.title: Feasible balanced biclique instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A balanced biclique instance $(n, es, K)$ is feasible when there are disjoint sets $A$ and $B$ of exactly $K$ vertices each in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that every vertex of $A$ is adjacent to every vertex of $B$, where distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ belongs to $es$. In other words, the graph contains a complete bipartite subgraph $K_{K,K}$, not necessarily induced.

results.title: The decision problem BALANCED BICLIQUE

results.summary: BALANCED BICLIQUE is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a balanced biclique instance $(n, es, K)$ that is well formed (the entries of $es$ are distinct, and every pair $(u, v)$ in $es$ has $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \neq v$ and $(v, u) \notin es$) and for which there are disjoint sets $A$ and $B$ of exactly $K$ vertices each in…

results.title: BALANCED BICLIQUE is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem BALANCED BICLIQUE belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.

results.title: Composing diagonal tests conjoins their assertions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Sequential tests conjoin their assertions without changing state.

results.title: Verification inequality characterizes partial correctness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The verification inequality is precisely universal partial correctness: every execution from `P` ends in `Q`.

results.title: Postcondition absorption characterizes partial correctness
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Partial correctness as unreachability of the negated postcondition

results.title: Test of the true assertion is the identity relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The true assertion is the identity relation.

results.title: Test of a negated assertion is the complement within identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Boolean test negation is complement relative to identity, not the full relation-algebra complement (which includes off-diagonal pairs).

results.title: Test of a union of assertions is the union of tests
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Union of assertions is union of their diagonal tests.
